judgments.reasoning_cat1: The insuring clause is a short promise to pay proceeds 'according to the following provisions'; it names no ambiguous term of its own beyond that open-ended incorporation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It defers wholly to Sections 2-10 (e.g. 4.1 Payment of Proceeds), so it is unlikely to contradict them, though it identifies the Owner as the counterparty consistent with 2.2.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A free-look clause with a fixed 20-day period and a stated address; 'void from the beginning' is definite and the refund is of 'any premium you have paid'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits comfortably beside 3.1 (premium at delivery) and 7.2 (effective date); no other provision addresses return of the policy within 20 days.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The paid-up benefit is truncated mid-list ('level amount based on: a. The current Policy Account Value less any Policy Indebtedness'), leaving the death benefit computation incomplete and its trigger ('anniversary following the Insured's 95th birthday') dependent on Age as defined only in a fragment.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It has to be reconciled with 4.2's greater-of death benefit formulas, the Section 1 maturity/termination date, and 5.3's continuing Monthly Insurance Charge, and the fit is not obvious.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The introduction is descriptive, but the sentence that Sections 3 through 10 give 'a more complete description' invites argument about which text governs a conflict.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That priority statement is exactly what would be invoked if a definition (e.g. 2.14 Coverage Options) diverges from the operative text (4.2), which it arguably does.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line definition of the Insured by reference to the person listed in Section 1; nothing in it carries two readings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It matches Section 1's schedule and 4.1's death-proceeds trigger without tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'You or Your' means the Owner listed in Section 1; the definition is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 8.1 Ownership and 8.2 Change of Ownership; no competing usage found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'We or Us' identifies the insurer by name; no ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used uniformly throughout the policy with no conflicting reference.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition is cut off but reads as beneficiary named in the original application, subject to later change; nothing independently ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 8.4 adds that if no beneficiary is named the Owner is beneficiary, a gap the definition does not mention, so the two must be read together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Proceeds' is defined to cover both death and surrender payments, which is workable though it lumps two different amounts under one label.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 4.1 distinguishes 'Surrender Value' from 'Death Proceeds' and Section 10 speaks of 'Policy Proceeds', so the defined term is used inconsistently across the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Policy Date is defined as the computation date shown in Section 1; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 2.17 (Monthly Due Date keyed to Policy Date) and 7.2 (effective date on the later of Policy Date or premium payment).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Effective Date: the date coverage commences' is short and its cross-references (Section 3.2 for the initial Policy) appear misdirected, since the initial effective date is fixed by 7.2.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The policy carries several date concepts — Policy Date, Effective Date, and the undefined 'Issue Date' used in 7.6 and 7.8 — and this definition does not reconcile them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Only a fragment survives ('upon the Insured's age on the birthday nearest the first ...'), so the definition of Age is incomplete on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Age drives the 4.2 risk-percentage table, the 5.4 cost-of-insurance table and the 95th-birthday paid-up benefit, so an incomplete definition has whole-instrument consequences.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause both says the Planned Periodic Premium is what you 'most recently elect to pay' and that during the first two years the scheduled amount 'is the minimum that must be paid', two ideas that sit awkwardly together.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 3.2(1) and 3.2(2) set out a different first-two-year test (monthly pro-rata accumulation), and 5.10's no-lapse rule uses yet another formulation of the same idea.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and definite: the Minimum Initial Premium must be paid before delivery and is shown in Section 1.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 3.1 says 'at or before the time this Policy is delivered' while this says 'before the date this Policy is delivered', a small divergence, and 7.2 makes payment an effective-date condition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The Specified Amount definition is heavily truncated but conveys an amount specified in the application, used to determine death benefit and changeable under 6.2.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coheres with 6.2 increases/decreases and 5.9's automatic reduction under Option A; no direct conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The amount to be paid, prior to any adjustment specified in Section 4' is a definition that depends entirely on another section, and the phrase 'prior to any adjustment' is not self-explanatory.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 4.2 in fact computes the death benefit as a greater-of, and 4.2's later paragraph adds rider and premium increases and indebtedness decreases, so 'Death Benefit' has more than one operative meaning across the policy (notably in 5.4's 'B').

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Both coverage options provide for an increased death benefit when the difference between the Policy Account Value and the death benefit reaches a minimum size' is vague — 'minimum size' is nowhere quantified here.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The definition says Option A pays 'the Specified Amount', but 4.2 makes it the greater of the Specified Amount (plus recent premiums with interest) or a corridor percentage of Account Value, so definition and operative text diverge.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition itself is clear: the monthly deduction covering cost of insurance plus rider costs.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It directs the reader to 'Section 4.3', but the Monthly Insurance Charge is in 5.3 (4.3 is Interest on Death Proceeds), a mis-cross-reference of the kind also seen in 3.4(2) and 5.1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The charge we make for providing pure insurance protection using the current Cost of Insurance rates' is definite enough, though 'pure insurance protection' is not defined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The cross-reference to 5.4 is correct and 5.4's formula matches; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Keying the Monthly Due Date to 'the same day of each month as shown in the Policy Date' leaves months lacking that day unaddressed, a small but real gap.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 5.3, 5.10 and 9.4 all turn on Monthly Due Dates, but none supplies the missing-day rule either; otherwise consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'There is no insurance coverage in effect until the payment is made' is an absolute statement of a condition precedent, and the alternative 'Planned Periodic Premium or Minimum Initial Premium' leaves which amount suffices unclear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 7.2 contemplates a Temporary Insurance Agreement given when the application is taken, which would provide coverage before the policy premium is paid — a direct tension with the no-coverage sentence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'You may make premium payments at any time and in any amount you choose subject to the following' is an introduction whose freedom is immediately qualified.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The four numbered limits (minimum remittance, insurer-imposed caps in 3.2(4), 3.3's tax cap) substantially cut down the freedom stated, which is how the sentence is meant to work.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The surviving text ('total of your premium payments during the first two policy years must be at least the Planned Periodic Premium') is a bare minimum test with no timing rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 3.2(2) and 5.10's first-two-year no-lapse paragraph state the same requirement in monthly pro-rata terms, so the three must be harmonised.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The pro-rata formula is detailed and arithmetically specific; the only softness is 'the balance of the Planned Periodic Premium'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its monthly accumulation test is repeated almost verbatim in 5.10's no-lapse paragraph but stated there net of withdrawals and indebtedness, so the two tests are not identical.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A flat rule tied to a Section 1 figure, with a unilateral right to change it on notice; definite though one-sided.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 2.9's statement that each payment must at least equal the Minimum Premium Remittance.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause gives the insurer discretion to set 'minimum and maximum limitations' and then says 'This will happen only if' the payment would increase the gap between death benefit and Account Value — a limiting sentence whose reach over the preceding sentences is unclear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps with 3.3's tax-driven premium limit and 6.2's insurability requirements for increases without saying which governs.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause cites TEFRA 1982 and 'Section 101F of the Internal Revenue Code of 1954 or any future applicable regulations', a citation that is inaccurate and open-ended.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with 3.2's freedom to pay any amount and with 4.2's tax-driven modification right, which the Owner may refuse — a combination that could frustrate this clause's purpose.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The reinstatement window ('within five years after the expiration of the Grace Period and prior to the surrender of the Policy') is legible but the sentence is scrambled, and 'the Grace Period ends without sufficient premiums' is the assumed trigger.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be squared with 5.10(2)'s statement that the Policy 'will terminate without value' at the end of the Grace Period, since a terminated policy is nonetheless reinstatable here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Only 'Receipt of evidence of insurability of the ...' survives; as a condition it is standard but incomplete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parallel to 6.2's 'evidence of insurability satisfactory to us'; no conflict identified.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definite requirement: premium sufficient for at least the next two Monthly Insurance Charges.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cites 'Section 5.2' for Monthly Insurance Charges, but that is the Interest Rate section — the charge is in 5.3, a cross-reference error repeated elsewhere in the policy.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Indebtedness existing at the end of the Grace Period is reinstated if unpaid; plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits 9.4's definition of Policy Indebtedness and 3.4(4)'s use of lapse-date values.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Using the values 'in effect when the Policy lapsed' is a clear rule, though it does not say how interest or charges for the lapse interval are handled.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against 5.10(2)'s 'terminate without value' and 5.8's crediting of interest to the date of payment, which may not fully cohere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence breaks off at 'will be the Month...', so the effective date of reinstatement is not stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Because reinstatement timing drives 5.3 charges and 7.8's two-year reinstatement contestability clock, the missing date matters to other provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short bar on reinstatement after surrender; unambiguous in substance.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Duplicates the 'prior to the surrender' limit already in the 3.4 introduction rather than conflicting with it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: As written, 'We will pay the Surrender Value to you if the Insured is living and this Policy is in force' states no requirement of a surrender request, which is not what is meant.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 5.8 makes surrender an elective act on written request with a six-month postponement right, so 4.1 read literally contradicts 5.8.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard spendthrift sentence qualified by 'to the extent permitted by law'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing else in the policy addresses creditors; 8.3's assignment rights are a different subject.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An introductory pointer that death proceeds depend on Specified Amount and Coverage Option shown in Section 1.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 2.13, 2.14 and the Option A/B formulas that follow.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The greater-of formula is arithmetically specified, but 'the risk percentage from the table below for the correct age' depends on the truncated Age definition and an OCR-damaged table.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It contradicts 2.14's simpler statement that Option A pays 'the Specified Amount at the time of death'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Same greater-of structure for Option B, with a garbled phrase ('prior to our coinciding with date of death') that muddies the measuring date.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 2.14 describes Option B as Specified Amount plus Account Value without the corridor alternative, a mismatch between definition and operative text.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Increasing death benefits 'by any premiums received after the date of death' is an odd rule, and under Option A it may double-count premiums already added by 4.2 A.1.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The indebtedness deduction repeats 9.4, and 5.10(3)'s deduction of unpaid premium from Proceeds is a further adjustment not mentioned here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The insurer may modify death benefits to comply with federal tax law but the Owner 'has the right to refuse any modification' — the consequence of refusal is left unstated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That refusal right can defeat 3.3's promise to keep the policy qualified as life insurance excludable from gross income, a genuine internal tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Interest 'at an annual rate determined by us but never less than the rate required by the state' is discretionary but floored, and the section number itself is inconsistent (4.9/4.3).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The floor is keyed to the state where the Insured resides, whereas 5.6 and 5.11 key minimum values to the state where the Policy is delivered — different reference states within one instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The core formula 'A + B + C - D - E' is stated but the definitions of the components are fragmentary and one is described as 'the Monthly Insurance Charge as described in Section 2', which is the definitions section.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Policy Account Value drives 5.6 Cash Value, 5.7 Surrender Value, 4.2's death benefit and 5.10's lapse test, so an unclear formula here propagates through the whole instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The parenthetical example is self-contradictory — '6% less 2 points equals 6%' — a mechanical error that changes the stated arithmetic of the loaned-portion crediting rate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interacts with 9.3's loan interest charge and 5.6's 'C' adjustment for excess interest, so the crediting rate on loaned value could be computed two ways.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The charge equals cost of insurance plus rider costs for the month just ended; simple, if OCR-damaged.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches 2.15's definition and 5.4's computation, except that 2.15 points to 'Section 4.3' for this provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The formula is said to apply 'on any Premium Due Date' — a term used nowhere else and inconsistent with the Monthly Due Date basis — and the guaranteed table is stated 'per $1,050'; rates are also set on 'our expectation of future experience', a classic point of contest.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 2.16, 2.17 and 5.3 all fix the charge to the Monthly Due Date, so this section's trigger date does not match the rest of the policy.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The special-risk adjustment survives only as fragments '(a) For a flat ... rating percentage; or (b) For a flat extra rating', leaving the adjustment mechanics unstated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 1 records the Insured as 'STANDARD', so the special-class adjustment may never engage; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pointer to Section 1 for rider costs; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 2.15 and 5.3, which both include rider costs in the monthly charge.
